answer.rationale: The write-path latency spike coincides with a security patch that cannot be rolled back. Memory_b1 confirms rollbacks clear checkout error spikes, but the compliance constraint makes that unavailable here. Memory_b5 shows that routing read-heavy report queries to read replicas relieves pressure on the primary, recovering write latency the same day. With settlement traffic at peak and writes heavy, we cannot afford to lose customer writes or cut over regions. Routing report/dashboard reads to replicas directly reduces load on the primary write path without touching the security patch, without requiring a regional shift under peak traffic, and without adding capacity that may take longer than the 90-minute degradation window allows. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against partner outages, not internal write-path saturation. Regional failover (memory_b2) is a bigger move than needed and risks settlement consistency at peak. Add_capacity is slower to spin up and doesn't address the root cause if the new release changed query patterns. Read-replica routing is the single intervention with the highest probability of recovering write-path latency while preserving all customer writes and keeping the mandated security patch in place.
